newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria takes urgent steps to secure grain sowing.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria takes urgent steps to secure grain sowing.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Friday approved a bill aimed at unblocking payments due to farmers from troubled banks in a bid to secure the autumn sowing and stave off further grain shortages, a deputy said on Friday.
"The parliament today approved a bill envisaging measures to speed up the delayed autumn sowing," Zlatimir Orsov, a deputy for the ruling Socialist Party, told Reuters.
Farmers have delayed sowing because of record high interest rates for loans and because their funds are blocked in banks placed under special supervision by the central bank.
Local newspapers say nearly four billion levs or some 80 percent of the funds belonging to farm cooperatives are blocked in those banks.

Under the bill, proposed by the Socialist majority in the parliament, the Bulgarian National Bank should give priority to unblocking payments due to co-operatives from the nine banks put under special supervision on September 23.

Central bank deputy governor Dimitar Dimitrov told parliament he supported the measures, though he added, "The funds blocked in banks under special supervision are not of crucial importance for solving the problem".
Only 200,000 ha of wheat and barley have been sown so far, which is some 15 percent of the planned 1.6 million ha needed to cover domestic consumption, state news agency BTA reported.

Under the bill, the purchase prices of wheat, maize and barley from the 1996-1997 harvest should not be below 80 percent of their international prices, a measure which Orsov said aimed to provide incentives for farmers.
The deputies also advised the cabinet to allow the export of no more than 50,000 tonnes of cooking oil.

Bulgaria, a traditionally agricultural country, has been suffering an acute grain shortage following excessive exports last year compounded by a poor harvest this summer due to adverse weather and a lack of funds.
Last year Bulgaria sowed one million ha with wheat and 270,000 ha with barley. -- Galina Sabeva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561 REUTER GDS TG
